chapter: Blanton, Los Angeles and Art Tatum
title: Charlie Parker as a person and his search for new sounds
summary: Parker was friendly; Stewart asked how he developed bebop and thinks Parker was as harmonically impressive as Tatum.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: But what kind of a guy did Charlie Parker strike you as? Did you get to know him very well?
Yes, wonderful person all the way around.
Yes, very friendly. We got along very good. And --
What I meant, asking you about Parker, what kinds of things did you talk to him about? I mean what kind of a personality did he have?

Well, we didn't have too much to talk about. Our styles of -- I would -- I have had -- I did ask him how did he go about developing that be-bop style of his. And, of course, I imagine, just like myself, he was searching for new ideas, new ways to approach the musical scene, in other words, not play the same old jazz all the time, but to get something different, something new.
Is that what he said when you asked him?
And so did he strike you -- how -- did he strike you as being as sophisticated harmonically as Tatum was?
Yes, he did. Yes. Although Tatum didn't play be-bop, it was -- he was -- Charlie was equally impressive with his style in be-bop as Tatum was with his style on the piano.
